source_refs.note: Topic 17.11 as printed with the three boxes (PDF 100-102, printed 96-98); Fig 17.10 redrawn.

blocks.text: Consider an AC circuit containing a resistor R and inductor L connected in series with an AC source V as shown in Fig.17.10(a). As R and L are in series, therefore, same current I flows through both R and L.

blocks.alt: (a) A resistor R and inductor L in series with an AC supply V (+ and -); current I flows round the circuit; double arrows mark VR across R and VL across L. (b) Voltage V and current I against omega t from 0 to 360 degrees, with the same period; V leads I by theta. (c) Vector diagram OABP: OA = VR along the current I (R), OB = AP = VL (XL = wL) at right angles, and the diagonal OP = V = IZ at angle theta.
blocks.caption: Figure 17.10: (a) RL series circuit connected with A.C. supply; (b) voltage and current waveform of RL series circuit; (c) vector diagram of VR and VL of RL series circuit (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 17.10).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 17.10(b) draws voltage and current 90° apart and at different frequencies, and (c) labels OA 'V'. Both have the same frequency, the voltage leads by θ (tan θ = ωL/R), and OA is V_R, as drawn above. The printed captions of (b) and (c) also read 'waveform in of' and 'VR and VL in of'; the stray 'in' is dropped in the caption above.

blocks.title: For your information
blocks.text: Electric Eels create powerful shocks by its 3 main organs consisting of 80% of Eels body length through specialized cells called electrolytes.

blocks.alt: An electric eel: a long dark eel with a pale belly curving through blue-green water above a sandy bottom, its mouth open to the left, with white electric sparks around its body.
blocks.caption: For your information: an electric eel (original drawing after the picture printed in the textbook's box).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The specialised cells of the electric eel are called electrocytes, not electrolytes (an electrolyte is a solution that conducts electricity).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The squares belong outside the brackets: Vᵣₘₛ = √((IᵣₘₛR)² + (IᵣₘₛX_L)²) = Iᵣₘₛ√(R² + X_L²), as the next line uses.

blocks.text_alt: As X_L = ωL, so Vᵣₘₛ = Iᵣₘₛ √(R² + (ωL)²)
